topic: Runway, Luma, Pika, Midjourney, Adobe, Stability, Genmo, Lightricks, Meta, Amazon, xAI: video-model milestones, 2023 to 2026-09-29

milestones.headline: Stability's first video foundation model: open image-to-video weights making 14- or 25-frame clips, released for research only.

specs.notes: Image-to-video only (cannot be controlled through text). Max ~4 s per the model card. Audio not stated. Research release: 'not intended for real-world or commercial applications at this stage'.

claims.claim: Companion paper arXiv 2311.15127 submitted 25 Nov 2023 (corroborates the year).
claims.quote: [Submitted on 25 Nov 2023]

claims.claim: Developer describes it as its first foundation model for generative video.
claims.quote: Today, we are releasing Stable Video Diffusion, our first foundation model for generative video based on the image model Stable Diffusion.

claims.claim: Two image-to-video models, 14 and 25 frames, 3-30 fps.
claims.quote: capable of generating 14 and 25 frames at customizable frame rates between 3 and 30 frames per second

claims.quote: trained to generate 25 frames at resolution 576x1024 given a context frame of the same size

milestones.headline: Multi-view diffusion model that turns 2D images into 3D-camera-controlled videos along user-defined or preset camera paths; non-commercial research preview.

specs.notes: Takes a single input image or up to 32; 14 preset dynamic camera paths (360, Lemniscate, Spiral, Dolly Zoom, Move, Pan, Roll). Research use under a Non-Commercial License.

claims.claim: Announcement page dated 'Mar 18' (year not printed).
claims.quote: Mar 18

claims.claim: Companion paper arXiv 2503.14489 submitted 18 Mar 2025 (corroborates the year).
claims.quote: [Submitted on 18 Mar 2025

claims.claim: Generates 3D videos following user-defined camera trajectories.
claims.quote: The model generates 3D videos from a single input image or up to 32, following user-defined camera trajectories

claims.claim: Research use only, Non-Commercial License.
claims.quote: available for research use under a Non-Commercial License

milestones.notes: Camera-control milestone for the 'more control' chapter; weights are non-commercial so not usable as reusable footage.

milestones.headline: Runway shows Gen-3 Alpha, first model on new large-scale multimodal infrastructure: better fidelity, consistency and motion than Gen-2, with fine temporal control.

specs.notes: Announcement page does not state clip length, resolution or fps. Page says the model 'will be released' and will power Text to Video, Image to Video and Text to Image.

corrections_to_common_beliefs: Runway Gen-3 Alpha: 17 June 2024 is the announcement ('will be released'); Runway's changelog dates text-to-video for paid plans 1 July 2024, image-to-video 29 July 2024, and Gen-3 Alpha Turbo 14 August 2024.

Runway Gen-4 (announced 31 March 2025, available to paid plans 1 April 2025) did not ship with References; the changelog dates Gen-4 References 30 April 2025 for paid plans, and an object-consistency update 25 June 2025.

Runway Gen-4.5 launched (1 Dec 2025; available to paid plans 11 Dec 2025) as text-to-video; first-frame image input arrived 21 Jan 2026. Its '#1 with 1,247 Elo' is a developer-cited leaderboard snapshot as of 30 Nov 2025, not a current or independent ranking, and Runway itself lists causal-reasoning, object-permanence and success-bias failures.
Runway Act-One was announced 22 Oct 2024 but rolled out gradually (changelog 25 Oct 2024).

Midjourney V1 Video (18 Jun 2025) is image-to-video only (no text-to-video), was web-only at launch, makes four 5-second clips per job extendable to 21 s, and defaults to 480p (720p HD on higher plans). Midjourney itself warns of 'wonky mistakes' and clips that do not move.

Luma Dream Machine's 12 June 2024 launch produced 5-second shots; Ray2 (15 Jan 2025) offered 5-10 s base clips extendable to 30 s. Luma's version line is Ray2, Ray3 (18 Sep 2025), Ray3.14 (26 Jan 2026), Ray3.2 (9 Jun 2026); no 'Ray4' was found. 'First reasoning model' and 'first 16-bit HDR' are Luma's own marketing claims.

Meta Movie Gen (4 Oct 2024) was a research announcement, never a public release: Meta wrote of 'a potential future release'. Meta Vibes (25 Sep 2025) is a feed, not a named video model, and Muse Video (7 Jul 2026) was only an 'early preview' with stated gaps.

Adobe's Firefly Video Model did not launch in one step: preview 11 Sep 2024, limited public beta 14 Oct 2024, public beta 12 Feb 2025 (five-second 1080p generations). By April 2026 Adobe calls Firefly an all-in-one studio with 30+ models, so 'made in Firefly' does not identify the model.
Amazon Nova Reel 1.1's 'two-minute videos' (7 Apr 2025) are multi-shot sequences stitched from 6-second shots, not one continuous 2-minute clip; Reel 1.0 (3 Dec 2024) was 6 s at 1280x720, 24 fps.

Stable Video Diffusion (21 Nov 2023) is image-to-video with 14 or 25 frames, cannot be steered by text, and was released for research use; Stable Virtual Camera (18 Mar 2025) is likewise non-commercial research.

'Open source' does not mean reusable footage: Mochi 1 is Apache 2.0 for the model; LTX-2 and LTX-2.x use custom community licences (license: other); none of the retrieved pages grants reuse rights for demo videos. Also LTX-2 was announced 23 Oct 2025 with weights promised 'later in 2025' but arrived January 2026.

Platform is not model: by Sep 2026 Pika (17 Sep 2026), Runway (Feb-Aug 2026 changelog), Adobe Firefly (Apr 2026) and Luma (6 Aug 2026) all host third-party models (e.g. Seedance 2.5, Wan 3.0, Kling 3.0, Sora 2 Pro, MiniMax H3). Every excerpt label must name the underlying model, not the app.

xAI's Grok Imagine Video 1.5 text-to-video is produced by text-to-image then image-to-video (per xAI docs); native 1080p, T2V and up to seven references arrived 31 Jul 2026, not at the 16 Jun 2026 general release.

Pika release days are only bracketed by archived site banners (Pika 2.2 exactly on 27 Feb 2025; 1.5, 2.0, 2.1, 2.5 to windows of 1-3 days), so treat month-level dates as safe and day-level dates as inferred except 2.2.
